'''Lasse Rempe''' (born 20 January 1978) is a German mathematician born in [[Kiel]].<ref name="LRCV"/> His research interests include [[holomorphic dynamics]] and [[holomorphic function|function theory]].<ref name="LRHP">{{cite web|url=https://personalpages.manchester.ac.uk/staff/lasse.rempe/|title=University Homepage|author=Lasse Rempe|accessdate=19 February 2025}}</ref> He currently holds the position of [[Professor]] of [[Pure Mathematics]] at the 
[[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester]].<ref name="LRHP"/>  He previously worked at the [[University of Liverpool]] from 2006 to 2024,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/people/lasse-rempe|title=Liverpool staff profile|author=Lasse Rempe|accessdate=19 February 2025}}</ref> holding the "Shipowners' Chair" of Pure Mathematics from 2020 to 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pcwww.liv.ac.uk/~lrempe/shipowners-chair.html|title=The "Shipowners' Chair" of Pure Mathematics|author=Lasse Rempe|accessdate=19 February 2025}}</ref>  Rempe recorded the voiceover for a [[BBC]] feature on the art of mathematics, where he explained how certain pictures have arisen from [[dynamical system]]s.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/7617191.stm|author=BBC News|title=The Art of Mathematics|access-date=October 9, 2010|date=September 16, 2008}}</ref>

==Name==
From 2012 to 2020, he used the name Lasse Rempe-Gillen.<ref>[https://zbmath.org/?q=ia%3Arempe-gillen.lasse Listing of Rempe's publications] in [[zbMATH]], retrieved 2024-07-17</ref>

==Early life and education==
Rempe earned his Master of Arts degree in mathematics from [[Stony Brook University|State University of New York at Stony Brook]] in 2000<ref name="LRCV">{{cite web|url=https://pcwww.liv.ac.uk/~lrempe/Papers/2015_03_LRG_CV.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|year=2015|publisher= University of Liverpool|access-date=2024-06-17}}</ref> and his doctorate at the [[University of Kiel]] in Germany.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|84048}}</ref>

== Awards ==

In June 2010, Rempe was awarded a [[Whitehead Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]] for his work in [[complex dynamics]], in particular his research on the [[escaping set]] for [[entire function]]s.<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=London Mathematical Society Newsletter|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/394%20-%20July%202010.pdf|issue=394|date=July 2010|title=LMS Prizes 2010|page=16}}</ref>

In 2012 he was awarded a [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/sites/default/files/imported_pdfs/2012%20prize%20winners%20+%20citations.pdf |title=Philip Leverhulme Prize Winners 2012 |access-date=2015-06-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402225750/https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/sites/default/files/imported_pdfs/2012%20prize%20winners%20+%20citations.pdf |archive-date=2018-04-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was elected as a member of the 2017 class of [[Fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to complex dynamics and function theory, and for communication of mathematical research to broader audiences".<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2017 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], [[American Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2016-11-06.</ref>
